claims.head: Korpisalo’s hold on the Flames won’t last
claims.body: Korpisalo has been a wall against the Flames since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Korpisalo isn’t that wall tonight.

story.head: Picky vs. trigger-happy
paras: The Rangers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Calgary on Nov 11. The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, and the Flames (11-14-2) lost 5-3 to New Jersey last night. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (24th in the NHL) and the Rangers fourth in the Metropolitan (18th).

The Flames’ record (.444) is about what their chances are worth. The Rangers have played better than their record (.540) says: their chances are worth about .612, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so the Rangers wait for good looks, but they settle for hopeful ones. Calgary has scored 2.59 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Rangers get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd), hit a lot (2nd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd).

Joel Farabee (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 27 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 27 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 26 A / 28 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring. Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals, with five goals in seven games against Calgary since 2023-24.

Dustin Wolf (6-6-2 / .878 SV% in 14 GS) is in line to start for Calgary. Joonas Korpisalo (3-1-0 / .912 SV% in 4 GS) has been terrific for the Rangers and will likely start. Korpisalo has a .929 save percentage in five starts against the Flames, well above his usual .889. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
